text:
Tristan Luneau has a point in eight straight games (four goals, seven assists) and become a real part of Anaheim's run. The Ducks have won five in a row with him playing nearly 20 minutes a night and four of his points coming on the power play, and his long-range power-play goal against Pittsburgh on Nov. 8 made it 4-0. For a 22-year-old with 14 NHL games before this season, that's a breakout.

Our form check calls the streak earned: he's getting more chances on his own shots than usual, not just collecting assists. The team is also far better with him on the ice, 54% of the expected goals at five on five and a big relative edge. But be realistic about the finishing. Four goals on 1.55 expected and a 17.4% shooting rate are well above what defencemen sustain, and Anaheim has scored more than expected with him out there. Expect fewer goals and more assists. Evolving-Hockey's only sample (125 minutes in 2023-24) was rough and is now ancient history. Our projection puts him near 49 points, which would make the 53rd pick in 2022 a steal.
